newsitem.title: INDIA: World Bank offers $325 mln for Indian irrigation.
newsitem.headline: World Bank offers $325 mln for Indian irrigation.

text.p: The World Bank on Wednesday announced a $325 million assistance package for an irrigation project in the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

The bank said in a statement released in the capital New Delhi that the package included a $175 million loan and a $150 million low-interest credit from its concessional lending arm, the International Development Association (IDA).
It said the project would boost Andhra Pradesh's agriculture sector and revamp part of its irrigation system. Andhra Pradesh's main crops include rice, oilseeds and cotton.
The project would increase the productivity of more than 310,000 hectares (766,010 acres) in the drought-prone region, raising the income of mostly marginal and small farmers, the bank said.
The project includes irrigation development, agricultural support service programmes, a resettlement programme, an environmental management plan and dam rehabilitation and safety assurance.
Andhra Pradesh will provide $152.43 million of the total $477.43 million in project costs, with the bank financing the rest.
The $175 million loan has a variable interest rate and a maturity of 20 years, including a five-year grace period. The credit is on standard IDA terms, with a 35-year maturity.
The Indian government will pass on the proceeds of the loan and credit to Andhra Pradesh.
